paper_metadata.title: A New Initial Distribution for Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks to Load Probability Distributions

summary: The paper proposes a label-replacement method for constructing shallow initial distributions for qGAN generators that can be implemented with single-qubit gates (depth d≈1 or effectively d=0). In classical simulation with 3 qubits and 8 discretized points, the method reduces relative entropy when learning distributions (e.g., ≈0.0016 mean KL divergence for log-normal targets with k=2) compared to uniform initialization and is competitive with normal-distribution initialization while requiring shallower circuits.

experiments.description: qGAN simulation study comparing a proposed shallow initial distribution (via label replacement) against uniform and normal initial distributions for learning log-normal, triangular, and bimodal target probability distributions.

algorithm.variant: quantum generative adversarial network (qGAN) with custom initial distribution / label replacement
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized Ry layers with interleaved CZ gates in the generator; initial distribution circuit uses single-qubit H or Ry gates
algorithm.parameter_initialization: generator initial weights randomly sampled from uniform [-1e-1, 1e-1]; proposed initial distribution encoded by fixed Ry angles derived from target distribution; uniform baseline via H gates; normal baseline via fixed Ry circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 8-point discretized probability distributions loaded into computational basis states; label replacement permutes measurement outcomes to match target ordering
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize relative entropy H(P|Q) between target distribution and generated distribution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported; label replacement is a classical relabeling of measurement outcomes rather than a quantum constraint method

problem_instance.description: Learning and loading probability distributions for qGAN-based state preparation relevant to quantum expectation estimation in finance

dataset_specification.description: target distributions: log-normal (mu=1, sigma=1), triangular (l=0, u=7, m=2), bimodal (two Gaussians with mu1=0.5, sigma1=1 and mu2=3.5, sigma2=0.5); 8-point discretization

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: samples drawn from each target distribution, discretized into 8 points; target probabilities sorted for label replacement initial distribution construction
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent training runs per initial distribution and target distribution; performance measured by mean, standard deviation, and minimum relative entropy over runs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: target distributions sampled and discretized; label replacement permutation computed from sorted probabilities; initial Ry angles derived analytically
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: relative entropy computed between generated and target distributions; best run selected for figure comparisons

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum expectation estimation / amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a general algorithmic claim from prior work, not a new empirical speedup shown in this paper.

speedup_claims.factor: up to O(2^n) gates for Grover-Rudolph state preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: for loading probability distributions into quantum states
speedup_claims.caveats: Used as motivation for shallow qGAN-based loading; not a measured speedup in the experiments.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: qGAN generator uses shallow circuits; paper emphasizes d=1 or d=0 initial distributions and contrasts with Grover-Rudolph O(2^n) state preparation
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo expectation estimation O(1/epsilon^2); Grover-Rudolph state preparation up to O(2^n) gates

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not quantified. The study only evaluates 3‑qubit circuits with 8 discretization points in classical simulation.
limiting_factors: Experiments only use 3 qubits and 8-point discretized distributions
All results obtained via noiseless classical simulation
No comparison to classical state-preparation or distribution-learning algorithms beyond internal qGAN initialization variants
No empirical speedup or runtime comparison measured
Practical usefulness depends on larger-scale amplitude-estimation workflows that are not demonstrated

notes: num_qubits inferred as 3 from the 8-point discretization and explicit references to 3-qubit circuits in the text; hardware is a Qiskit simulation with no real QPU named, so simulator_other is inferred from context.

The paper does not claim experimental quantum advantage; it motivates the work using the known quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation (O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε²)) but only studies initialization strategies for qGAN state preparation.
The experiment compares different initial distributions within the same qGAN framework rather than quantum vs classical algorithms.
